report.summary: Chunk 4 of 6 for daedalus/structcore/artifacts.py: defines Column, ArtifactSchema, schema readers for csv/json/npy, and constants OPTIONAL_READERS and SCHEMA_FROM_CODE.
risks: Column.to_dict | low | Returns dict with keys name, dtype, shape; no validation that these are set. | Ensure all fields are always populated or handle missing.

ArtifactSchema.known | medium | Property returns True only if status == READ; comment says empty columns on NOT_SUPPORTED is 'we did not look', but code does not enforce that. | Add a check that columns are empty when status is NOT_SUPPORTED?
ArtifactSchema.to_dict | low | Returns 'known' key derived from property; could be cached or cause side effects if property changes. | Ensure property is stable.
_csv_schema | medium | Uses csv.Sniffer().sniff() which may be slow or raise on edge cases; catch csv.Error but not other exceptions. | Consider broader exception handling.
_csv_schema | medium | Parses only first line; assumes header row exists; no handling for quoted fields with newlines. | Add note about limitations.
_json_schema | low | For list of dicts, uses first record's keys; comment says later records may differ, but no check. | Add validation or note.
_npy_schema | medium | Regex parsing of NPY header; relies on latin1 decode; may fail on malformed but non-malicious headers. | Consider using numpy if available.
read_schema | high | Function signature and docstring present but body not in this chunk; cannot verify behavior. | Complete implementation in next chunk.
OPTIONAL_READERS | low | Dict of format->library; no validation that libraries are installed. | Document that missing libraries cause fallback.
SCHEMA_FROM_CODE | low | Set to NOT_SUPPORTED constant; comment says 'Not implemented' but code is clear. | No action needed.
todos: Complete read_schema implementation in next chunk.

Consider adding type hints for all functions.

claims.text: True only when the schema was actually read. An empty column list on a NOT_SUPPORTED artefact is not 'no columns' — it is 'we did not look'.
claims.why: Property returns self.status == READ; status is READ only when schema was read. The docstring claim matches code.

claims.text: A bounded read can truncate valid JSON, so say which it was.
claims.why: The function returns detail with 'bounded MAX_SCHEMA_BYTES-byte read may have cut it'.

claims.text: NPY header, parsed with struct — the format is documented and stable.
claims.why: Function uses struct.unpack to parse header lengths and decode header.

claims.text: Schema for one artefact from a BOUNDED read of its head. Never the payload. The caller does the I/O and passes at most MAX_SCHEMA_BYTES; this keeps the module pure and testable, and keeps the read bound in one place.
claims.why: Docstring claims about function behavior; function body not in this chunk.

claims.text: Formats whose schema needs a reader this module does not carry. Named so the report can say WHICH dependency would light each one up, instead of a blanket 'unsupported'.
claims.why: Comment accurately describes the constant's purpose.

claims.text: Tier-1 hook: schema as declared in code (TTree::Branch, read_csv(names=)). Not implemented. Named so its absence is visible rather than assumed away.
claims.why: Constant is set to NOT_SUPPORTED, indicating not implemented.

observations.what: Column.to_dict returns a dict with keys name, dtype, shape; no validation that these are set.
ArtifactSchema.known property only checks status == READ; does not enforce that columns are empty when status is NOT_SUPPORTED.

_csv_schema only parses first line; assumes header row exists; no handling for quoted fields with newlines.
_json_schema for list of dicts uses first record's keys; comment notes later records may differ, but no validation.
